summary:
Astro Flame is an SI-powered web dashboard designed to bridge the gap between decades of NASA combustion research and the critical fire safety needs of future space exploration. Historically, disasters like Apollo 1 demonstrated the fatal consequences of material flammability in high-oxygen environments. Today, as engineers design the Moon Base—where oxygen levels make materials >40% more flammable than on Earth—the challenge isn't a lack of data, but the overwhelming volume of it. NASA’s PSI database contains hundreds of experiments, yet it is scattered and impossible to interpret during a crisis.

Astro Flame solves this by combining semantic search, grounded AI summarization, and physics-based predictive modeling. Engineers like our persona "Alex" can ask plain-language questions and instantly receive 3-line AI summaries (strictly grounded in PSI text to prevent hallucination) and smart-ranked results. Most importantly, Astro Flame features a real-time "Flight-Safety Assessment" simulator that predicts sustained-burn risks and extinction probabilities for specific materials.

By turning complex microgravity data into 30-second actionable insights, Astro Flame ensures that the next giant leap—to the Moon and Mars—is a safe one. Because safety can't wait, and data shouldn't either.
details:
What it does & How it works:

Astro Flame is an SI-powered interactive dashboard built to help engineers quickly navigate NASA's massive Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database. Users can input plain-language queries (e.g., "Which fabric is safe at 30% oxygen?"). Our system uses semantic search to find relevant experiments, followed by a strictly grounded LLM that generates 3-line summaries to prevent AI hallucination. It then ranks results based on material type and environment. The dashboard also features a "Flight-Safety Assessment" simulator that visually predicts sustained-burn risks and extinction probabilities.

Benefits & Impact:

Astronauts and engineers designing the Moon Base and Mars missions currently face a critical bottleneck: data is scattered and impossible to interpret in a crisis. Astro Flame reduces this search time from days to 30 seconds. It provides actionable, evidence-based insights for fire prevention, ensuring that materials chosen for space habitats are safe under extreme oxygen conditions.

Tools & Technologies Used:

Python, Streamlit (Frontend), FAISS/ChromaDB (Vector Search), Sentence-Transformers (Embeddings), LLMs (with strict prompt engineering for grounded summarization), and NASA PSI datasets (Saffire, BASS, FLEX).

Creativity & Considerations:

Our main creative approach was putting the user (our persona "Alex") at the center of the design. We considered the severe risks of AI hallucination in safety-critical scenarios, which is why we enforced a "side-by-side" verification UI (showing the original NASA text next to the AI summary). We also considered the UX by designing the interface as a "Mission Control" dashboard to make complex data feel intuitive and actionable.
